question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>CNG</mi></math> is an important transportation fuel. When <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi>gCNG</mi></math> is mixed with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>208</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> oxygen in vehicles, it leads to the formation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></math> and produces large quantity of heat during this combustion, then the amount of carbon dioxide, produced in grams is [nearest integer] [Assume CNG to be methane]

solution.text:
CH4+   2O2⟶   CO2+2H2O

10016    20832

Number of molesstoichiometric coefficient for CH4=6.251  Number of molesstoichiometric coefficient for O2=6.52=3.25

The reagent with lower ratio of number of moles to stoichiometric coefficient is called limiting reagent.

Hence, O2 is limiting reagent

Limiting reagent decides the amount of product,

As per the equation 2 moles of O2 gives rise to 1 mole of CO2, So 6.5 moles of O2 gives 6.52 moles of CO2

⇒nCO2=6.52

So mass of CO2=6.52×44=143gm
